section_1.title: The Problem: Why Old Models Forget
section_1.content: Introduce the limitation of sequential processing (RNNs). Explain that as sentences grow, early information fades. Use a prerequisite visual: a 'conveyor belt' vs. a 'cocktail party'.
section_1.example: A reader tries to memorize a 100-page book by reading one word at a time, forgetting the start by the time they reach the end.

section_2.title: The Intuition: The Cocktail Party Effect
section_2.content: Explain that Attention allows the model to look at all words simultaneously and decide which are relevant to the current word. Visual: Connecting lines of varying thickness between words in a sentence.
section_2.example: In the sentence 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired,' when the model processes 'it', it draws a thick 'attention' line to 'animal' and a thin one to 'street'.

section_3.title: The Mechanism: Queries, Keys, and Values
section_3.content: Break down the core math into an analogy: A library system. Query (what I want), Key (what the book label says), Value (the content of the book). Visual: A search bar searching for a specific book tag.
section_3.example: You (Query) look at book labels (Keys) to find the content (Value) that matches your request.

section_4.title: The Math: Dot-Product Attention
section_4.content: Simplify the mathematical operation: Score = Q × Kᵀ. Explain the Softmax function as a way to convert scores into percentages (weights). Visual: A heatmap showing intensity values that sum to 100%.
section_4.example: If the Query 'it' matches 'animal' with high intensity, the model assigns 0.9 weight to 'animal' and 0.1 to 'street'.

section_5.title: Application: Contextual Understanding
section_5.content: Summarize how this enables LLMs to generate coherent text. By weighing inputs, the model understands polysemy (words with multiple meanings) and long-range dependencies.
section_5.example: An AI assistant reading a manual: 'The robot picked up the wrench because it was heavy.' Attention ensures the AI knows the *wrench* is heavy, not the *robot*.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        lines = [
